subject: FinBridge: suspected token exposure and notification path
messages:
From: Martin Klein <m.klein@finbridge.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>; kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@finbridge.com; LegalOps <legalops@finbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Possible token exposure - quick heads up

Hi Irene / Kimberly,

Apologies for the early message. Our security operations team picked up what looks like an API token that was accidentally posted in a third-party error log. The token appears to be scoped to a short-lived ingestion key for a demo environment but shows calls to an endpoint that maps to your inference-hosted API.

We're not finished triaging on our side, but we wanted to notify you promptly per our DPA obligations. I've attached a short log excerpt (finbridge_log_excerpt_0428.txt) and a one-page summary (evidence_summary_v1.pdf).

Can you confirm:
- Whether that token would let someone access customer data or only demo/test payloads.
- Whether Redwood considers this an incident under the DPA trigger (48-hour notify window) or a lower-severity operational alert.

We also need to understand what data types were touched (IDs, email addresses, embeddings, etc.) and whether any subprocessors were involved in handling the affected workload.

Thanks — Martin
Security Ops, FinBridge

---
Attachments: finbridge_log_excerpt_0428.txt (text excerpt), evidence_summary_v1.pdf (summary)

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Martin Klein <m.klein@finbridge.com>; LegalOps <legalops@finbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible token exposure - quick heads up

Hi Martin — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. We appreciate the rapid notification.

Quick answers and initial asks:
- We will treat this as a potential DPA notification candidate until triage proves otherwise. Our standard is to assume potential exposure of personal data where production keys or customer-bound endpoints are implicated.
- Ben (security) will evaluate whether the token scope would allow access to customer-identifiable data or only demo/test streams.
- Kimberly (privacy) will confirm the notification thresholds under FinBridge's DPA and whether this meets the 48-hour window.

Please:
1) Confirm the earliest timestamp in the attached excerpt and whether FinBridge has identified any outbound exfiltration beyond the posted log.
2) If you have a list of affected customer IDs or dataset labels, share a redacted summary (hashed IDs are fine).
3) Share any runbooks or subprocessors that might have processed the same ingestion key (if different infra teams were involved).

We will send a formal acknowledgement and provisional timeline within 4 hours and a fuller update within 24 hours.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
Note: internal recipients only; provisional classification pending security determination.

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>; kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Martin Klein <m.klein@finbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible token exposure - quick heads up

I pulled the excerpt and ran it against our ingestion logs. Preliminary notes:
- The token in the excerpt maps to an ingestion key we issue for ephemeral QA environments. The key's auth scope should only allow writes to the demo tenant; it doesn't grant access to production customer payloads.
- However, the request path shown includes a dataset label that matches "fb-prod-search-2026" — that suggests a mislabeling on FinBridge's side or replay of a scrubbed payload.
- No downstream data export (S3 export or external webhook) shows matching hashes in our outbound telemetry.

Next steps I'm initiating:
- Rotate any keys that match the fingerprint within 2 hours and revoke related ephemeral tokens.
- Snapshot KV cache and request logs (retention holds) for the 72-hour window mentioned in the DPA so Legal can review possible PII touchpoints.
- Stand up a shared evidence folder (I created the Drive link in the metadata) and invite FinBridge SOC.

Ben
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: none (log excerpt included from external message)

From: Martin Klein <m.klein@finbridge.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@finbridge.com>; security-team@finbridge.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 12:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible token exposure - quick heads up

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick triage. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The dataset label was an internal tag; we are still confirming whether the payload was production-origin. We do have a redacted sample with hashed IDs — attaching it to this thread now.
- We have a DocuSign link for a small data transfer authorization that our procurement/legal team requested while we confirm scope (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/s/FinBridge-Redwood-evidence-access).

Would Redwood be comfortable proceeding with:
1) Temporary evidence access (view-only) for FinBridge LegalOps to validate that no PII was present.
2) If PII is identified, coordinate a formal 48-hour DPA notification with a proposed joint statement.

Martin

---
Attachment: finbridge_redacted_sample_hashes.txt

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Martin Klein <m.klein@finbridge.com>; irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible token exposure - quick heads up

Martin — thanks for the sample and the DocuSign link. Redwood is willing to provide time-bound, view-only access to the evidence folder while we jointly confirm scope. We will: 
- Put a preservation hold on the relevant request logs and KV cache (Ben coordinating).
- Invite FinBridge LegalOps to the Drive folder with view-only rights; we will not export or share PII externally.
- If the redacted hashes prove to map to customer-affiliated identifiers, we will treat it as a DPA incident and begin drafting a joint notification. We will align proposed language with your LegalOps team prior to external communication.

Please confirm the names/emails for FinBridge reviewers to add to the folder and whether you want Redwood to lead the joint notification draft or to co-author. Also confirm any subprocessors on FinBridge's side involved in ingestion so we can map cross-processor obligations.

Thanks — Kimberly
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference

---
Action items (internal):
- Ben: complete key rotation + retention snapshot by EOD.
- Irene & Marissa: prep provisional notification templates and escalation ladder (if PII confirmed).
- LegalOps (FinBridge): confirm reviewer list and sign DocuSign if required.
